title: Break the filters
brief: Numbers beat opinions. Starve a post-filter, squeeze a pre-filter's recall, leak a revoked grant, then look for the copies of your data that live outside the ACL: caches and logs.

blocks.intro: Teaching simplification, not a benchmark. Relevance is assumed independent of permission, so candidates are exchangeable and a post-filter sees visible documents in proportion to the visible fraction. Start with the three presets (broad access, group based, per document), then run the three guided experiments under the results: starve the post-filter, squeeze the pre-filter's recall, and compare sync lag with a live check.

blocks.title: Over-fetch for a post-filter

vars.v: visible fraction, the share of the corpus the caller may see

blocks.example: At f = 2% and k_needed = 10, fetch **500** candidates. In the simulator's group-based preset (f = 5%, k = 10, 3x over-fetch) the post-filter returns a median of 1 result and about 22% of queries are empty. Source: the lab model, a hypergeometric draw.

blocks.title: Chance a grant is stale inside the sync window

vars.v: revocations per grant per hour, the daily revocation rate divided by 24
hours between the change at the source and the index

blocks.example: At 5% revocations a day and 24 hours of lag, P(stale) is about **4.9%** per returned grant. With 10 hits per query, 1 - (1 - 0.049)^10 is about **39%** of queries that include a revoked document. Source: the lab model.

blocks.title: Cache options for permissioned content
blocks.intro: Every cache is a second copy of the answer. Its key and its TTL decide who can read it and for how long after a revocation.

options.name: No cache
options.summary: Generate every answer from a fresh, filtered retrieval.
cons: Full generation cost and latency every time
options.bestWhen: ACL scope is nearly unique per user, or the content is in a restricted tier.
options.avoidWhen: Heavy repeat traffic over broad, shared access.

options.name: Exact-match response cache keyed by ACL scope
options.summary: Key on the normalized question plus the caller's scope (user or group set).
cons: Hit rate falls as the scope key gets finer
TTL must stay below the revocation SLA
Needs purge on document or ACL change
options.bestWhen: Repeated questions inside large groups with identical visibility.
options.avoidWhen: The key is the question alone, which hands any user any cached answer.

options.name: Semantic cache with `vary-by`
options.summary: Match similar questions, but only inside a partition. Azure API Management partitions with `vary-by`, for example on user or group id.
cons: The docs warn it can return incorrect, outdated or unsafe answers
Should be skipped when any source document is restricted (design reasoning)
options.bestWhen: FAQ-like traffic over broad shared content.
options.avoidWhen: Restricted content, or scope that is nearly unique per user, where it is cost with little benefit.

options.name: Provider prompt cache only
options.summary: Rely on the provider's prefix cache and add nothing of your own.
pros: Scoped by the provider: per organization (OpenAI), per subscription (Azure OpenAI, [[r30]]), per workspace on several Anthropic surfaces
cons: Saves cost and latency only on repeated prefixes
`prompt_cache_key` is for routing and accounting, not a security control

An ICML 2025 audit found timing side channels where caches were shared across users in seven providers. Provider docs state scoped caches as of 2026-10-13, so read the paper as the reason to prefer scope [[r29]]
options.bestWhen: A safe baseline for every tenant.

blocks.caption: Logging policy. Logs copy ACL-protected content into a store that has no ACLs.
head: Policy
Keeps
Debugging power
Risk
rows: Document ids, principal id, filter hash, outcome
Reproduce which documents and which filter, not the text
Lowest. Matches the advice for access logs of grounding data and immutable retrieval logs [[r22]] [[r2]]
Redaction misses things, and the log store needs its own access control
Prompts, chunks and answers for a bounded window
Protected text lives outside the ACL. Set retention and deletion rules

items.symptom: A revoked user keeps the same answer for 25 minutes after the index ACL changed in 2 minutes.
items.cause: A response or semantic cache entry whose TTL is longer than the revocation SLA, or whose key ignores ACL scope.
items.fix: Key by ACL scope, keep TTL below the SLA and purge on document and ACL change events.

items.symptom: A user gets an answer built from a document they cannot open.
items.cause: A semantic cache shared across users that matched on similarity with a loose threshold.
items.fix: Partition with `vary-by`, tighten `score-threshold` (the docs suggest starting near 0.05) and skip the cache for restricted labels [[r28]].

items.symptom: Support staff can read confidential snippets in the trace viewer.
items.cause: Full content logged to a store with broader access than the source system.
items.fix: Log ids and decisions. Capture content only for a bounded window with its own access control. Stateful features such as the Responses API and stored completions also hold prompts at rest in your Foundry resource, so include them in retention and deletion rules [[r38]].

items.symptom: Deleted documents still appear in answers.
items.cause: Tombstones never reached the index, the semantic cache or a stored answer.
items.fix: Propagate deletes to every copy and verify with a canary document that you delete on purpose.

quiz.q: A caller can see 2% of the corpus and you need 10 results after a post-filter. About how many candidates must you fetch?
quiz.explain: 10 divided by 0.02 is 500. Fetching fewer returns fewer than 10 results for most callers, and fetching 500 costs latency and sends 490 denied documents through your code, rerankers and logs. That is why selective access points to a pre-filter.

quiz.q: Revocations run at 2% of grants a day and the sync lag is 12 hours. A query returns 10 hits. About what percent of such queries include at least one revoked document?
quiz.hint: P(stale) = 1 - exp(-lambda x lag), then 1 - (1 - P)^10
quiz.explain: lambda is 0.02 / 24 per hour, so lambda times 12 hours is 0.01 and P(stale) is about 0.995% per grant. Over 10 hits, 1 - (1 - 0.00995)^10 is about 9.5%. A small per-grant rate still leaks in roughly 1 query in 10, which is why a live check on the top hits is worth its latency for restricted tiers.

quiz.q: Select every cache design that keeps ACL-protected answers from crossing between users.
options: An exact-match response cache keyed by the normalized question only
A semantic cache partitioned with `vary-by` on the group set, with a TTL below the revocation SLA
The provider's prompt cache, which matches identical prefixes inside one organization or subscription
A semantic cache shared by all tenants with `score-threshold` 0.3
quiz.explain: Partitioning by group set with a short TTL keeps answers inside one visibility scope. Provider prefix caches are scoped per organization or subscription and only hit on identical prefixes. A question-only key serves one user's answer to another, and a shared semantic cache with a loose threshold can match unrelated questions across tenants.

quiz.q: A user was removed from a group at 10:00. The index ACL updated by 10:02, yet the user saw the same restricted answer until 10:28. Which cause fits the log?

code.code:
response_cache: key=sha256(question) created=09:58:12 ttl=1800s
index_acl_update: doc-77 groups -= [finance] at 10:02:03

options: The indexer interval is set to 30 minutes, so the ACL change arrived late
The access token still carries the old groups claim until it refreshes
A 30 minute response cache keyed by question
The reranker cached its scores for the old result set
quiz.explain: The cache entry was created at 09:58 with a 1,800 second TTL, which expires at 10:28, and its key ignores who asked. The index ACL changed at 10:02, so the indexer was not the delay. A stale token claim would affect who is resolved, not replay a stored answer, and a reranker cache would not return finished answer text.

takeaways: Selective access starves a post-filter: fetch about k_needed divided by the visible fraction, or filter inside the query.
A pre-filter keeps results full but filtered ANN recall drops. Measure it at your real selectivity.
Even a 2% daily revocation rate leaks in roughly 1 query in 10 at 12 hours of lag. Live-check restricted tiers.
Caches and logs are copies. Key caches by ACL scope, keep TTLs below the revocation SLA and log ids, not content.
Provider prompt caches are scoped per organization, subscription or workspace. Use `prompt_cache_key` for routing, not security.
